title: Rollback executor: revert canary/A-B traffic splits safely (step-down, rate limits, idempotency)
author: Jada Williams
description: Context: As part of the Auto-rollback on SLO breach integration, the rollout controller needs a rollback executor that can safely revert traffic splits for both canary and A/B rollouts. The current controller supports pausing a rollout step, but rollback execution was manual and non-idempotent, which is risky during incident mitigation and can cause oscillation/over-shifts when actions are retried. This PR implements the rollback executor with rate-limited traffic shifts, a step-down strategy, and strict idempotency semantics. Summary of changes: (1) Introduce RollbackExecutor with a deterministic plan generator that computes a sequence of traffic-shift steps to revert to baseline (or last-known-good) with bounded per-step delta; (2) Add idempotency keys at the action layer to guarantee that retries (controller restarts, at-least-once evaluation triggers) do not double-apply shifts; (3) Add guardrails: max shift per minute, minimum dwell time between steps, and abort conditions when telemetry indicates the split is already at target; (4) Add explicit handling for partial failures (policy engine timeout, traffic router 409 conflicts) with safe backoff and resume; (5) Emit structured audit events + metrics hooks (wired but behind feature flag; actual metrics/alerting added in follow-up PRs). Behavior: For canary rollouts, rollback shifts traffic from canary->baseline using step-down (e.g., 20%->10%->5%->0%), respecting rate limits and requiring a consistent read of current split before each step. For A/B tests, rollback targets the baseline arm (A) and rebalances traffic while preserving the pinned assignment semantics (no per-user reassignment changes; only the router weights). Rollback is idempotent per (rollout_id, step_id, action_type, target_split_hash). If the executor is invoked twice with the same target, it becomes a no-op after verifying current router state. Feature flag: rollout.auto_rollback.executor_v2 (default off). Related: ENG-4829; pairs with PR-28411 (SLO evaluator hook) and PR-28463 (debounce/min-sample). Notes for reviewers: The bulk of the logic is in rollout/controller/rollback_executor.go and router client idempotency is implemented via X-Idempotency-Key + action ledger table. Tests include deterministic simulation of concurrent invocations and router conflict responses. Risk: Medium. Changes are isolated behind flag; rollout execution now persists an action ledger row even for no-op idempotent retries (for auditability).
commits: rollouts: add rollback executor interface + initial canary rollback plan generator
router: add idempotency key support + conflict retry policy
rollouts: implement step-down + rate-limit guardrails for traffic shifts
rollouts: action ledger persistence + idempotent apply semantics
tests: simulation harness for rollback retries, conflicts, and partial failures
docs: inline godoc + controller config defaults (flagged)
notable_snippets: Planner step-down example: target=0%, max_step_delta=10% -> [current 25% -> 15% -> 5% -> 0%] with min_dwell=60s and max_shift_per_minute enforced.
Idempotency key: sha256("rollback|<rollout_id>|<step_id>|<target_split_hash>|<policy_version>") sent to router and persisted in action_ledger for de-dupe across restarts.
Safe no-op: if router reports weights already within epsilon of target, executor records an audit event "rollback_already_at_target" and returns success without shifting.
review_conversation: Jordan Lee (review): Can you clarify what happens if the router state drifts between steps (e.g., manual operator tweak) while rollback is mid-flight? I'd prefer we re-read current weights before each step and re-plan.

Jada Williams (author): Yep—updated executor to re-read router weights each step and re-compute remaining plan from the live state. Added test rollback_replans_on_drift; also tightened max step delta bounds so replan can’t jump >configured cap.
Benji Okafor (review): Action ledger schema: do we need policy_version + config_hash stored for audit? Also ensure uniqueness constraint is on idempotency_key not rollout_id alone.
Jada Williams (author): Added policy_version + policy_hash columns and a UNIQUE(idempotency_key) constraint. Also storing target_split_hash and router_scope to disambiguate multi-region runs.

Sean Gallagher (review): For incident safety, we need a hard cap on total rollback duration; otherwise step-down + dwell could take too long while SLO is burning. Can we allow an 'expedite' mode when triggered by SLO breach, while still rate limiting?

Jada Williams (author): Added max_total_duration (default 6m) with a safety behavior: if remaining steps would exceed cap, we compress dwell times down to min_dwell_floor (10s) but still enforce max_shift_per_minute. Also surfaced this as a policy knob (guardrailed).
Connor O'Brien (review): Migration looks fine but please confirm backfill behavior in staging. Also, is the flag default off in prod? Release train needs a clear enablement note.

Jada Williams (author): Confirmed: no backfill required (new table only). Flag remains off by default everywhere; enablement will be done via ENG-4850 staged plan. Added release note text in PR description and linked Linear.

Chloe Martin (review): API surface: rollback executor returns detailed status; ensure Console doesn’t depend on these fields yet. Also please standardize error codes for router conflict vs policy engine timeouts.

Jada Williams (author): Kept status fields internal for now. Normalized errors into RolloutActionError{code, retryable, message}. Added codes ROUTER_CONFLICT, ROUTER_UNAVAILABLE, POLICY_TIMEOUT, LEDGER_CONSTRAINT.
